payload.title: hyp builds the store layer every layout needs
payload.body:
Part of #138; the layout, one view over every store, is #168, which builds on this. The candidate is a hyp commit; go test on its base and on the candidate is the instrument. The texts ride on this Goal as a prose-only change (PR #165): skills/hyp-prototype step 2 and README.md say to run hyp init where the repository's agent instructions say trees live, or at the repository root when they name none; AGENTS.md says a new Goal goes in the store that holds the Goal it continues, otherwise in a new investigations/<topic>/, and that a PR whose events file conflicts on GitHub is merged locally first, taking main's .tree/.gitattributes before git merge origin/main. The spec changes in the same PR: replay-spec §1, §2 and §6, sandbox-spec, and an ADR amending 0020. Out of this Goal: a patch naming a path under .tree/ together with --store; a hyp check warning for a store whose .gitattributes lacks the union line; an older pinned hyp reading a live union-merged store, which is accepted and stated in the ADR; and a store below a base's root, which #168 covers.

May change: hyp in this repository (cmd/, internal/, docs/), as commits on one local branch pushed as a PR the run never merges
May change: the hyp init placement texts in skills/hyp-prototype/SKILL.md, README.md and AGENTS.md, and any other text in skills/, README.md or AGENTS.md the change makes wrong
May change: a .tree/.gitattributes in each store under investigations/, and the events and evidence of this Goal's store, investigations/checkpoint-store
Read only: the events of every other store under investigations/; every frozen recipe version under recipes/
Never: run hyp init at the repository root
Never: replace the installed hyp binary at ~/.local/bin/hyp
Never: merge the PR

lines.text: [P] On a base commit whose root holds `.tree`, `hyp sandbox create --store SRC --cut EVENT` succeeds; the clone's `.tree` then holds the store cut of SRC at EVENT and no other file of the base's `.tree`: `hyp status` in the clone prints what `hyp status --as-of EVENT` prints in SRC, and the clone's `.tree/evidence` holds no folder of an Experiment added after EVENT.
[N] `hyp init` in a directory from which store discovery finds a store, at it or above it, is refused with exit 1, names that store's directory, and creates nothing.

[P] Store discovery walks up from the current directory and stops at the first directory that holds `.git`: when no directory from the current one up to that one holds a store, a command reports no store (exit 3) even when a directory above it holds one. With no `.git` at or above, it walks to the filesystem root.

[P] Replay orders events by id, then by actor, whatever the line order inside an events file: a store whose events files hold the same lines in another order prints the same `hyp status` and `hyp check`, and its store cut at the same event writes the same bytes, each events file's kept lines in id order.
[P] An appended event's id sorts after every event id the store holds, also when the clock reads earlier than the newest event.

[P] `hyp init` writes `.tree/.gitattributes` holding exactly the line `events/*.jsonl merge=union`; with it, `git merge` of two branches that each appended to the same actor's events file exits 0 and leaves that file holding every line of both branches once and no other line.

payload.title: hyp reads a repository's stores as one history, with the owner's overview and Goal relations as filters
payload.body:
Part of #168, which continues #138. The candidate is a hyp commit; go test on its base and on the candidate is the instrument, and line 9 is a command record of hyp check on the candidate, kept by the Experiment that closes it. Decided in the grill of 2026-11-13: the repository has one history, every event of every store, ordered by id; stores stay in their folders (investigations/<topic>/.tree) and no event moves; the store an event belongs to is the folder of its events file, and no event stores it; an alias is a name local to its store, since a rubric's verdict label binds to a Hypothesis by alias and arms reuse labels such as h-null; the owner's overview is hyp status --all. Accepted: a hyp built before this change, reading one store that cites another, rejects that cite; across branches, ids keep only the order ADR 0022 gives. The specs change in the same PR: replay-spec §1, §2, §5, §6 and §8, sandbox-spec §5.3, the glossary's Store, Tree, Cite and Store cut, and an ADR amending 0020 and 0022; a <name>:ID token stays unchecked prose for a tree outside the repository.

May change: hyp in this repository (cmd/, internal/, docs/), as commits on one local branch pushed as a PR the run never merges
May change: any text in skills/, README.md or AGENTS.md the change makes wrong
May change: the events and evidence of this Goal's store, investigations/checkpoint-store
Read only: the events and evidence of every other store under investigations/; every frozen recipe version under recipes/ and investigations/*/recipes/
Never: run hyp init at the repository root
Never: edit or remove a line of any events file
Never: replace the installed hyp binary at ~/.local/bin/hyp
Never: merge the PR

lines.text: [P] `hyp status` run in a folder where store discovery finds a store shows only the Goals of the store in that folder, and a Goal is held by the store whose events file holds its add.

[P] `hyp status --all`, run anywhere in the repository, and plain `hyp status` where store discovery finds no store, list every Goal of the history and every item awaiting the owner, grouped by Goal. `hyp status` given a Goal's id, run anywhere in the repository, prints what it prints in the folder of the store that holds that Goal.

[N] A store adds nothing to the history when git tracks none of its events files, or when it sits under another store's `.tree/`, under a `testdata/` directory, under a bundle's `known-answers/`, or under a directory below the repository root that holds its own `.git`. With no `.git` at or above the current directory, the history is the one store discovery finds.

[P] A Goal line's `--cite` and a reading's `of` may name a key of a Goal in another store of the history; each is checked settled at its place in the history, and refused with exit 1 when it is not. `hyp show` given a Goal's id lists the Goals it cites and the Goals that cite it.
[P] An appended event's id sorts after every event id the history holds when the append takes its lock, in one clone, also when two actors append to two stores at once.
[N] A history whose stores hold one event id twice is rejected on replay at the later line, ordered by id, then actor, then the store's path, then the line's bytes.

[P] Two stores may hold the same alias. An alias resolves among the nodes of the store found from the current folder, and a cited verdict label among those of its Result's store; where it names nodes of two stores it is `ambiguous node` with exit 2. An alias used twice in one store is still refused at write and rejected on replay.

[N] An event never crosses stores: it is appended to the store that holds its node. A node add whose parent, or a Result, select, edge, refer or checkpoint whose node or key, lies in another store is refused with exit 1 and rejected on replay; an answer whose keys lie in two stores, and `hyp add goal` where store discovery finds no store, are refused with exit 1, naming the rule.
[P] On the candidate, `hyp check` at the repository root reads this repository's five stores under investigations/ as the history and reports 0 rejected events.

[P] `hyp sandbox create --cut EVENT` without `--store` gives a clone where each store of the host's history holds, in its own folder, exactly the history's events at or before EVENT, and no evidence folder of an Experiment added after EVENT; a store of the base that holds no such event is not in the clone.
